oewn/oewn-2025.status: In the catalog (story-bible-and-import-ux-briefs.prd.md Phase 7, ADR 0097); the reader's Look up panel shows it (Phase 8)
oewn/oewn-2025.note: Open English WordNet 2025 JSON release. Licence read 2026-09-23 from the repository's LICENSE.md: CC BY 4.0 for OEWN, with attribution to both Princeton WordNet and the OEWN team. Pinned by SHA-256 and size (a GitHub release asset URL can be re-uploaded, so a changed file fails the check and is refused); the bytes were downloaded and hashed on 2026-09-23 and match the digest GitHub reports for the asset. The install unpacks it and keeps only a lookup index built from it (about 17 MB); the attribution is shown with every lookup and printed in the third-party notices.

wiktextract/wiktextract-en-pronunciation.commercialUse: Pending (per upstream docs, not verified in this session: CC BY-SA 4.0 and GFDL dual licence, share-alike, attribution required; ADR 0405 accepts the class, scoped to displayed IPA only)
wiktextract/wiktextract-en-pronunciation.status: In the catalog as a Pending row (prep-depth Phase 8, ADR 0405); its URL and SHA-256 are not yet filled in because the egress proxy blocks kaikki.org, en.wiktionary.org and every candidate mirror this session could try (docs/research/wiktextract-pronunciation-source.md, #510); Install/Repair refuse the row until a future session verifies it
wiktextract/wiktextract-en-pronunciation.note: Wiktionary's IPA data, extracted and republished as structured JSON Lines by the Wiktextract project (kaikki.org). Licence terms restated from Wiktionary's and Wiktextract's own public documentation, not re-read live this session (docs/research/wiktextract-pronunciation-source.md). Once installed, the derived index keeps only a word -> {ipa, audio} lookup file, never the raw multi-gigabyte release; every displayed answer carries a CC BY-SA attribution label and the full notice is printed in the third-party notices.

ffmpeg/ffmpeg-7.1-essentials-win64.commercialUse: Yes (GPL-3.0-or-later build of FFmpeg; encoding an audiobook with it does not put the audiobook under the GPL)
ffmpeg/ffmpeg-7.1-essentials-win64.status: In the catalog (render-encode-master.prd.md Phase 1, ADR 0342, Proposed); the MP3 encoder runs it as a separate process
ffmpeg/ffmpeg-7.1-essentials-win64.note: FFmpeg 7.1 essentials build by gyan.dev, from the imageio-ffmpeg 0.6.0 win_amd64 wheel on PyPI (a content-addressed URL; the SHA-256 is PyPI's published digest, checked 2026-09-27). The install keeps only ffmpeg.exe, and only when its own SHA-256 is the pinned one. Build configuration read from the binary: --enable-gpl --enable-version3, no nonfree; the paths the app uses (libmp3lame, the WAV reader, the MP3 muxer) are LGPL code. Windows only. The project does not convey it (PyPI does); the notices name the licence and where the source is (docs/research/ffmpeg-encoder-build.md).
